clue.text: Doctor, one breaking smart fellow's chemistry apparatus

indicators.note: the doctor and the one break into the smart fellow, splitting his name open

parts.note: a smart Alec is a know-all, so the fellow is ALEC
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A doctor barges in on a clever man's lab equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal but is a medical degree; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old distilling vessel used by alchemists and early chemists, so a piece of laboratory equipment.

clue.text: Aussie PM visiting Qatar voluntarily

indicators.note: the answer pays a visit to these words, staying inside them

explanation.surface: An Australian prime minister makes a voluntary trip to Qatar.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is not prime minister but post meridiem, the afternoon, in Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for afternoon, the hours abbreviated PM.

clue.text: Free verse optionally used for literary work

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are set loose to fall in another order

explanation.surface: Free verse is optionally used in literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free verse' looks like a poetry term; 'Free' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel told through letters, such as Dracula or Clarissa, a type of literary work.

clue.text: Romantic German queen in her cups?

indicators.note: the queen goes inside her cups

parts.note: bras are what hold a woman's cups
HM, Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A sentimental German monarch who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In her cups' is an idiom for drunk; read literally the cups are a bra's. Johannes Brahms was a composer of the Romantic era.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms was a German composer of the Romantic period in music.

clue.text: Commanding Officers running for shelter

parts.note: CO stands for Commanding Officer, and the plural gives two of them
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Senior officers dash for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A silky case spun by a larva protects it, and by extension any protective covering or refuge.

clue.text: Political enforcer saying something cutting

parts.note: a party whip keeps MPs voting the party line
a saw is an old proverb or saying

explanation.surface: A party heavy comes out with a sharp, wounding remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something cutting' suggests a barbed comment; it is literally a tool for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow-bladed saw tensioned in a frame, a tool whose job is cutting timber.

clue.text: Not pink, but in the pink, having put on top from Etam

parts.note: in the pink is an idiom for in good health, well
to don clothing is to put it on

indicators.note: top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Healthy and looking good in a top bought at the store Etam.
explanation.walkthrough: Etam is a women's clothing chain, so 'top' plays on a garment. 'Not pink' is about steak, cooked through.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked thoroughly has no pinkness left in the middle.

clue.text: Person singing is playing well, with little uncertainty

parts.note: a player on good form is in form
er is a small hesitant noise of doubt

explanation.surface: A singer in good voice who has only a slight hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is slang for informing to the police, so the singer is a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sings to the police, a grass, passes on information about criminals.

clue.text: Acclaim temporary government, one working to introduce zero tax

indicators.note: the zero tax comes first, introducing what follows it

parts.note: a stand-in is a temporary substitute
O looks like zero
VAT, value added tax
I is the Roman numeral one
a working machine is on

explanation.surface: Praise for a caretaker government whose member brings in a zero tax rate.
explanation.definitionFit: When an audience rises to its feet to applaud, it gives a performer enthusiastic acclaim.

clue.text: Spending two days gardening with inside knowledge

indicators.note: the knowledge sits inside the gardening

parts.note: weeding is a gardening job
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: A weekend spent gardening by someone in the know.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending Saturday and Sunday away somewhere, a short break of two days.

clue.text: Behold Victoria and Albert's framed painting

indicators.note: the two initials sit either side of the painting like a frame around it

parts.note: V is the initial of Victoria
A is the initial of Albert
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: Look at the canvas hanging in the Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is a London museum; here the names just give their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing used to present something with a flourish, much like saying look or there it is.

clue.text: Following complaint, stitch up something to keep plants warm

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first, following it

parts.note: a cold is a minor illness or complaint
to stitch someone up is to frame them for a crime

explanation.surface: After catching a cold, someone sews up a garden cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' reads as sewing, but it is slang for falsely incriminating.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-topped box in the garden that shelters seedlings and tender plants from frost.

clue.text: Street crossing through radio village, where blues will be playing

indicators.note: the crossing passes through the village, so it sits inside its name

parts.note: Ambridge is the village in The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap
a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: Directions to a road crossing that runs through a village heard on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea football club play in blue, so 'blues' is the team, not music or sadness; this is their London home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC, nicknamed the Blues, play their home matches at this stadium in west London.

clue.text: Ex-PM: a bluff, brooding character

parts.note: Edward Heath was British prime minister 1970-74
a bluff is a steep cliff or headland

explanation.surface: A former prime minister who is gruff, dour and moody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' reads as blunt in manner; it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The brooding hero of Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights, a dark romantic figure.

clue.text: Other versions of the jazz singer

parts.note: EL is the Spanish form of the word that follows, one foreign version
LA is the French feminine word for the, another foreign version

explanation.surface: Cover versions of a famous jazz vocalist's songs.
explanation.walkthrough: The versions are of the word 'the': EL in Spanish and LA in French, Italian or Spanish. The singer is Ella Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Fitzgerald was a celebrated American jazz vocalist, known as the First Lady of Song.

clue.text: Shut up trainee journalist

parts.note: an intern is a trainee on a work placement
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: An order to silence a junior reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like a command to be quiet; it means locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: To be interned is to be confined or imprisoned, especially in wartime, so shut up in the sense of locked away.

clue.text: Struggles to breathe after getting pinched in tight clothes

indicators.note: the struggles come after the pinched goods

parts.note: hot goods are stolen, pinched
pants is gasps for breath

explanation.surface: Someone gasping after being squeezed into close-fitting outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' suggests squeezed; here it means stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Very short, tight shorts worn by women, a fashion item of figure-hugging clothing.

clue.text: Give better weapons to East German after all

parts.note: to rearm is to equip again with new weapons
OST is the German word for east

explanation.surface: Supplying better arms to East Germany after everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' looks like a filler phrase meaning nonetheless; it is the definition, behind all others.
explanation.definitionFit: The last in line, furthest to the back, coming behind every other one.

clue.text: Painter captures nothing, very upset

indicators.note: the painter's name holds the other letters inside it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: J M W Turner, the English landscape painter
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An artist manages to paint nothing at all and is very distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' is not distress but the act of knocking over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to tip or overturn it, so a turnover is an upsetting.

clue.text: Time off, taking time off

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, paired with the later off
off completes taking off, the instruction to remove a letter

parts.note: something off is not on, cancelled

explanation.surface: A spell of leave, during which someone takes some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT ON loses its T to leave the midday hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a particular time of day.

clue.text: Refuse to sleep with guy at university

parts.note: a guy is a supporting rope, also called a stay
a student is up at university

explanation.surface: Staying awake to be with a man at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man; it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Not going to bed, keeping awake late into the night.

clue.text: Fit for sport and runs

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of, for
PE, physical education, school sport
R stands for runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Fit enough for sport and running.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit and proper are both suitable or appropriate.

clue.text: Criminal is in patrol car, admitting love for plotting

indicators.note: the jumbled letters let love in, admitting it among them
criminal suggests the letters are bent or crooked out of shape

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A crook sits in a police car, letting slip a confession of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the person in the car; it is the anagram signal for IS IN PATROL CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting together, as in a conspiracy, describes a scheming manner or a knowing, secretive tone.

clue.text: Part of flight out of a prison

indicators.note: the a is taken out of the word

parts.note: a stair is one step in a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: Part of an escape from a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests escape, fitting the prison; it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Record's popular air and tracks about love

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vent lets air through, and to vent is to air
love is zero in tennis, written O
RY, short for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: A hit record's catchy tune and songs about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' reads as a music disc, matching air and tracks; it is a list. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete list of goods or property, an itemised account or record.

clue.text: Show some beer, getting a round in

indicators.note: the round goes in the drink

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Display a beer while buying a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A round' suggests buying drinks; it is just the circle O.
explanation.definitionFit: To show the way is to point it out, so show and point are synonyms as verbs of indicating.

clue.text: Mist mostly left to dissipate, shooting stars seen here?

indicators.note: to dissipate is to scatter, so the letters are scattered
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fog clears, revealing meteors streaking across the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: MIS (most of 'Mist') and LEFT are scattered. 'Shooting stars' are not meteors but filming celebrities, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A film set is where actors are filmed, so film stars being shot by cameras are found there.

clue.text: Other half of ripped carpet sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are written in the reverse direction

parts.note: rent is the old past form of rend, ripped
to carpet someone is to rap them, to reprimand

explanation.surface: Half of a torn rug returned to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb meaning to scold, not a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's other half is their spouse or long-term companion, a jocular idiom.
